text:
Judd Caulfield took the long road. A fifth-round pick of the Penguins in 2019, he went through North Dakota and the AHL's San Diego Gulls before getting his first NHL game this fall at 25. Twenty-three games in, he has four goals, 11 points and 86 hits, and Anaheim keeps giving him more: his ice time is up 3:38 a night over his last ten, and with Leo Carlsson out he has moved onto the first power-play unit.

Those ten games have been a grind on the scoresheet, no goals in eleven and three points where we'd expect about 5.4. But this is the kind of cold spell we like to see: his chances are holding at his usual rate (2.7 expected goals on his own shots), the pucks just aren't going in. For the season he has four goals on 6.0 expected. The five-on-five numbers are modest (44% of the expected goals), on a Ducks team that is losing. Our range projects 33 to 57 points. The hits make the case for keeping him in the lineup; the power-play time is his chance to make it for scoring.
